count.value: 15 social media sites tested in 2016 and 2013 (research page); about a dozen checked regularly (2019 page)

count.quote: The IPTC Photo Metadata Working Group tested 15 social media sites in 2016 and 2013

rows.name: IPTC Metawatch
rows.provenance_object: the lead photograph of a news article, as served to the reader
rows.provenance_carrier: embedded metadata (Exif, IPTC IIM and XMP) and C2PA manifests
rows.unit: a news publisher, sampled each month through up to 20 recent articles
transformations_tested: publication through a news site's pipeline (CMS, CDN, image optimisation)
rows.retention_results: October 2026: 7.2% of editorial images carried a credit or copyright notice (IMATAG's 2018 test: 8%); 321 of 425 crawlable publishers kept none of the scored IPTC fields; 27 of 6,580 images carried a C2PA manifest
rows.cadence: monthly, on the first of each month
rows.data_access: every run published as open data
negative_tags: NOT the 2019 IPTC social-media test: it measures news publishers monthly
NOT a C2PA verifier

self_description.quote: a free, open monitor that checks every month whether more than 500 news publishers in 122 countries keep the credits, captions and rights information embedded in their photographs

count.quote: On the first of each month our well-behaved crawler visits 508 news publishers in 122 countries, takes up to 20 recent articles from each, and reads the lead photograph of every article.

license.quote: every run is published as open data under CC BY 4.0

retention_results.quote: In 2018 IMATAG found that 8% of editorial images carried a credit or copyright notice. Applying the same test to our October run gives 7.2%.

retention_results_2.quote: In the October run, 321 of the 425 publishers we could crawl, three out of four kept none of the IPTC fields we score on any image we sampled.

transformations_tested.quote: Stripping appears to happen in the publishing pipeline, which means that publishers can fix it.

c2pa.quote: Leaving out IPTC’s own site, 27 of the 6,580 images we analysed carried a C2PA manifest

lineage_note.quote: Metawatch builds on IMATAG’s 2018 State of Image Metadata study and IPTC’s own prototype crawler from 2019

access_limit.quote: AP and USA Today began blocking automated access this month. It is a reminder that bot-blocking aimed at AI also shuts out research.
